la:verb:induco.html:
in-dūco, xi, ctum, 3 (
imp. induce for induc, ; induxti for induxisti,; induxis for induxeris,), v. a.
in-duco
, to lead, bring, or conduct into a place; to lead or bring in (class.); constr. with in and acc., dat., acc. only, or absol.
Lit.
With in and acc.: oves et armenta in rura,: aliquem in viam,: exercitum in Macedoniam,: cohortem praetoriam in medios hostes,: principes in cornua inducit,leads against,; so, Hannibal elephantos in primam aciem induci jussit,: in dextrum cornu elephantos,; —
With dat. (mostly poet. and rare): age, moenibus induc,: fossā mare urbi,. —
With acc. only: princeps turmas inducit Asilas,: inducunt venti nubilum,.—
Absol.: eā (portā) secundae legionis principes hastatosque inducit (sc. in urbem),.—
In partic.
To bring forward, exhibit, represent in the circus or on the stage: a me autem gladiatorum par nobilissimum inducitur,; so, aliquem,: elephantos in circum,: inducta est et Afranii Togata, quae Incendium inscribitur,; ; ; ; cf.: pater ille, Terenti fabula quem miserum vixisse Inducit,.—
To bring into or before a court (post-Aug.): inducta teste in senatu,: Firminus inductus in senatum,: majestatis reos in curiam,.—
To bring home, take into one's family: carasque toris inducere Thressas,: intra undecim dies quam illi novercam amore captus induxerat,. —
Transf.
To put on articles of dress: si sibi calceus perperam induceretur,: umeros albenti amictu,: togam super membra,. —With Gr. acc.: tunicāque inducitur artus,. —
To draw over, spread over, to overlay, overspread: postes pice,; : colorem picturae,i. e. to varnish,: parieti ceram liquefactam,: cuti nitorem,: varias plumas,: humanam membris formam,: omnibus viris magnitudine sua inducturus caliginem,to overspread with darkness, to darken, obscure,: pontem,to throw a bridge across,: scuta ex cortice facta pellibus,to cover,: coria super lateres,: pulvis velut nube inducta omnia inpleverat,: sed quae mutatis inducitur tot medicaminibus,.— With Gr. acc.: (victima) inducta cornibus aurum,; .—
To level the ground by filling up: ita inducto solo, ut nulla vestigia exstent,; hence, to strike out, erase, i. e. to level the wax in writing by drawing over it the broad end of the style: nomina jam facta sunt: sed vel induci, vel mutari possunt,: senatus consultum,.
Trop.
In gen., to bring into, introduce: seditionem atque discordiam in civitatem,: aliquid in nostros mores,: set magna pars morem hunc induxerunt, : morem novorum judiciorum in rem publicam,; ; : novum verbum in linguam Latinam,: pecuniam in rationem,to bring into, set down in an account,: agrum alicui pecunia ingenti, to charge in an account, : exemplum,.—
To establish: sublato judicum nomine potestas regalis inducta est,: quia nondum haec consuetudo erat inducta, § 4: vetus disciplina deserta, nova inducta,.—
In partic.
To bring in, introduce in speaking or writing (an expression borrowed from the stage): hinc ille Gyges inducitur a Platone,: gravem personam,: Tiresiam deplorantem caecitatem suam,.—Of conversation, to introduce: puero me hic sermo inducitur,: hanc rationem Epicurus induxit,: consuetudinem,: dubitationem,.—
To lead to or into; to move, excite, persuade; to mislead, seduce; constr. with in, with acc. or ad, with ut or inf.: amici jacentem animum excitare, et inducere in spem cogitationemque meliorem,; so, aliquem in spem,: in rem utilem,; cf. : in errorem,: animum ad aliquid,: aliquem pretio, gratia, spe, promissis (ad parricidium),to mislead,: multos in peccatum,to seduce,: ad maleficium,: ad misericordiam, ad pudendum, ad pigendum,to move, excite,: Carthaginienses ad bellum,: ad credendum,: vide, quo me inducas,: in quos (affectus) inducendus est judex,.—With ut: aliquem, ut mentiatur,.—With inf.: consulem promissis, sententiam promere,.—
Animum or in animum, to bring one's mind to, to resolve, determine; to suppose, imagine: id quod animum induxerat paulisper non tenuit,. — With inf. or object-clause: animum inducere, contra ea quae a me disputantur de divinatione, dicere,: opes contemnere,: id me commissurum ne animum induxeris,: in animum inducunt suum, Jovem se placare posse,: ne tute incommodam rem, ut quaequest, in animum induces pati?: oro ut ne illis animum inducas credere,: qui huic animum assentari induxeris,: mea causa causam hanc justam esse animum inducite,; cf. : ut in animum induceret ad easdem venire epulas,; ; : postremo Caesar in animum induxerat, laborare, vigilare,had determined,: in animum, ejus vitam defendere,; .—With ut, ne, or quominus: inducere animum possum, ne aegre patiar,: inducere animum, ut patrem esse sese, oblivisceretur,: in animum, quo minus illi indicarem,: quod consules in senatu ut pronuntiarent, in animum inducere non possent,; ; . —
To delude, cajole, deceive: hic eos, quibus erat ignotus, decepit, fefellit, induxit,: socios induxit, decepit, destituit,: semper, ut inducar, blandos offers mihi vultus .—
To do any thing to one (post-class.): injuriam adversus liberos suos testamento,.— Hence, in-ductus, a, um, P. a., introduced, foreign, strange (post-Aug. and rare): insiticius et inductus sermo (opp. patrius),; so, nihil inductum et quasi devium loquimur,: arcessita et inducta,.

la:adv:inde.html:
inde, adv.
i-im, locative from is, and de = die; hence

Of place, from that place, thence: inde e promptuaria cella,: si quis me quaeret, inde me vocatote aliqui,: eo die mansi Calibus: inde has litteras dedi,: ut in provinciam exirent, atque inde in Italiam contenderent,: nec inde venit, unde mallem,: Palaepolis fuit haud procul inde ubi nunc Neapolis sita est,: triginta inde stadia abesse,: si legiones sese recepissent inde quo temere essent progressae,. —With gen. loci (poet.): inde loci,; ; Enn. ap. Müll.; id. ap. .—
Of things: ex avaritia erumpat audacia necesse est: inde omnia scelera gignuntur,from this,: inde est, quod, etc.,.—
Of persons: nati filii Duo: inde ego hunc majorem adoptavi mihi,of them,: in Dacos et inde in Parthos,: nihil inde (i. e. ab iis) praesidii,: rege inde sumpto (i. e. ex Sabinis),—
Of time.
Prop., from that time, thenceforward, since (mostly preceded by jam): suo jam inde vivere ingenio coepit,: inde durat ad nos usque vehementer,.— So of time continued from a point referred to: inde ab ineunte aetate,; : inde usque amicus fuit mihi a puero puer,: jam inde ab ortu,: quoad longissime potest mens mea respicere spatium praeteriti temporis . . . inde usque repetens, etc.,; .—
In gen., after that, thereafter, thereupon, then (cf. deinde), ; ; : ne perorandi quidem ei data est facultas: inde judicio damnatus,: exhinc Rhaeticum bellum, inde Pannonicum, inde Germanicum gessit,then . . . then,: eodem impetu altera castra sunt adorti, inde tertia, deinceps reliqua,.—
With other specifications of time: jam inde a principio hujus imperii, Prov. Cons. 13, 33: jam inde ab incunabulis, —
With gen.: inde loci (transferred to time),after that, thereupon,.

in-dĭco, āvi, ātum, āre, v. a. (indicasso, is, for indicavero, is, ; ),
to point out, indicate (class.).
In gen., to show, declare, disclose, make known, reveal, betray.
Of persons: rem omnem dominae indicavit,: Catilina non se purgavit, sed indicavit,: conscios delendae tyrannidis,: jam me vobis indicabo, will betray or accuse myself, : indicabo meum consilium tibi,: rem patri,: causam publicae pestis,: de conjuratione,to give information, inform,: quis tibi de epistulis istis indicavit,; : aliquid in vulgus,to make publicly known,: satis est actori sic indicare,.—With rel. clause: contentus indicare quid facti sit,.—With acc. and inf.: digitis ita figuratis ut temporis et aevi (Janum) esse deum indicent,.—
Of things concr. and abstr.: vultus indicat mores,shows, indicates,; : lacrimis dolorem,: hoc res ipsa indicat,: id esse verum parva haec fabella indicat,: supercilia maxime indicant factum,: ut epularum sollemnium fides ac tibiae ... indicant,. — Pass.: aetas veterinorum indicatur dentibus,: cum res non gesta indicatur, sed ut sit gesta ostenditur,. —
In partic.
To intimate, give a hint of, to state briefly, mention: indicare convenit, quae prodit Onesicritus,: aliquid obiter,: nominatim,: ut indicavimus,.—
To set or tell the price of a thing, to value, put a price on: hanc eme. Do. Modo ut sciam, quanti indicet, etc., : indica, fac pretium,: cum postulasset, ut sibi fundus semel indicaretur,. —
In jurid. Lat., to carry on a judicial process to conviction: Indicasse est detulisse, arguisse, accusasse et convicisse,.

la:adj:indignus.html:
in-dignus, a, um, adj.,
unworthy, undeserving (class.).
Of persons.
In gen., unworthy.
Absol.: divitias quivis quamvis indignus, habere potest,: indignissimi candidati,—
With abl.: te omni honore indignissimum judicat. ; so ; ; ; ; —
With gen.: magnorum haud umquam indignus avorum,.—
With qui: iine indigni erant qui impetrarent?; so ; : indignus quem mors tam saeva maneret,— (ε) With ut: cum indigni, ut a vobis redimeremur, visi simus,.—(ζ) With inf.: indigni ( = quos non decet) fraternum rumpere foedus,; .—
Esp., not deserving any thing, undeserving: Indignis si male dicitur, male dictum id esse duco,: ad calamitates hominum indignorum (sc. istis calamitatibus) sublevandas,undeservedly suffering,: Pompeius morte,: cur eget indignus quisquam te divite,: indignus injuriā hac,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things.
Unworthy, unbecoming, shameful, intolerable, severe, cruel, harsh: ne istuc nequiquam dixeris tam indignum dictum in me,: nulla vox est audita populi R. majestate indigna,: nihil, quod ipsis esset indignum, committebant,: lictoribus indignum in modum mulcatis,: indignis modis acceptus,: facinus,: exempla,: mors,: aliquid pro indignissimo habere,: hoc uno sol quicquam non vidit indignius,: studiis indignum ferre laborem,: hiemes,severe,: fortuna,. — With the sup. in u: digna atque indigna relatu Vociferans,; .—With inf.: fabula non indigna referri,; : indignum est a pari vinci, aut superiore: indignius ab inferiore,: non indignum videtur, egregium facinus memorare,improper,: nonne hoc indignissimum est?; .—Absol.: indignum, as an exclamation,shame,; ; —
Undeserved: indigna pati,: indignamque necem pretium patietur amoris?.—Advv.: indignē and indignĭter.
Indigne.
Unworthily, undeservedly, dishonorably, shamefully: indigne dotem quaerere,: meretricem deperit,: aliquem injuria afficere,: cervices in carcere frangebantur indignissime civium R.,: interierunt,.—

index, dĭcis, com.

la:verb:indulgeo.html:
indulgĕo, si, tum, 2, v. n. and a.
[etym. dub.; cf. dulcis], to be courteous or complaisant; to be kind, tender, indulgent to; to be pleased with or inclined to, to give one's self up to, yield to, indulge in a thing (as joy or grief); to concede, grant, allow.
V. n. (class.); constr. with the dat.
In gen.: Aeduorum civitati Caesar praecipue indulserat,; : sic sibi indulsit, ut, etc.,indulged himself so, took such liberties,: indulgebat sibi liberalius, quam, ut, etc.,: irae,: indulgent sibi latius ipsi,: ipsa sibi imbecillitas indulget,: indulgent consules legionum ardori,: dolori,: genio,: amori,: precibus,: gaudio,: desiderio alicujus,: odio,: lacrimis,: animo, to give way to passion or to anger, : regno,to delight in,: ordinibus,give room to, set apart,.—
With acc. of the person (ante-class. and poet.): eri, qui nos tantopere indulgent, Afran. ap. (Fragm. Com. v. 390 Rib.): te indulgebant,; .—Pass.: animus indulgeri potuisset, be pleased, Gell. praef. 1.—
Esp., to give one's self up to, to be given or addicted to, to indulge in: veteres amicitias spernere, indulgere novis,: labori,: theatris,: eloquentiae,: somno,.—Pass. impers.: nihil relicturus, si aviditati indulgeretur, quod in aerarium referret,: sero petentibus non indulgebitur,.—
V. a., to concede, allow, grant, permit, give, bestow as a favor, confer (post- Aug.): alicui usum pecuniae,: ornamenta consularia procuratoribus,: damnatis arbitrium mortis,: insignia triumphi indulsit Caesar,: patientiam flagello,i. e. to submit to patiently,: nil animis in corpora juris natura indulget,grants no power,: basia plectro,: si forte indulsit cura soporem,: veniam pueris,to make allowance for,.—
With inf. (poet.): incolere templa,.— Pass.: qui jam nunc sanguinem meum sibi indulgeri aequum censet,: rerum ipsa natura in eo quod indulsisse homini videtur, etc.,: abolitio reorum, quae publice indulgetur,is granted,. —
Se alicui, in mal. part., —Hence, indulgens, entis, P. a.
Indulgent, kind, or tender to one, fond of one; constr. with dat., or in with acc. (class.).
With dat.: obsequium peccatis indulgens praecipitem amicum ferri sinit,.—
With in and acc.: civitas minime in captivos indulgens,. —
Absol.: quo ipsum nomen amantius, indulgentiusque maternum, hoc illius matris singulare scelus,: ministri irarum,. —
Addicted to: aleae indulgens,addicted to dicing,.—
In pass., fondly loved: fili, indulgentissime adulescens, Ps.-.— Adv.: indulgenter, indulgently, kindly, tenderly: nimis indulgenter loqui,: bestiae multa faciunt indulgenter,. — Comp.: dii alios indulgentius tractant,.— Sup.: indulgentissime,.

la:adj:indifferens.html:
in-diffĕrens, entis, adj.,
in which there is no difference, indifferent.
Act., of persons, making no difference, indifferent, careless (post-class.): circa victum,.—
Pass.
Philos. t. t., neither good nor evil, not to be sought or avoided (class.): necesse est, nec bonum esse nec malum hoc quod praepositum vel praecipuum nominamus; idque ita definimus, quod sit indifferens cum aestimatione mediocri; quod enim illi ἀδιάφορον dicunt, id mihi ita occurrit ut indifferens dicerem, : nihil indifferens gloriosum est; mors autem gloriosum est; ergo mors non est indifferens,.—Hence, subst.: indiffĕrens, ntis, n., a thing indifferent, neither good nor evil: si valetudo indifferens est, bene valere indifferens est,: cur dolor apud Stoicos indifferens esse dicitur, non malum,: Zeno censuit voluptatem esse indifferens, id est neutrum, neque bonum neque malum,.—Plur.: haec quae indifferentia vocamus,—
In gram., of the syllaba anceps, doubtful, ; .—Hence, adv.: in-diffĕrenter, without distinction, indiscriminately, indifferently (post-Aug.): uti utraque appellatione,; : uti his litteris,: ferre, to bear with indifference, unconcern; opp. graviter, : vivere,to eat of everything without distinction,.
